question: On the same registered units and grades, do conventional methods notice when the evidence channel cannot support a bilateral certification decision?

channels.name: confounded
channels.note: preregistered natural-confounding construction; did not collide

channels.name: adversarial
channels.note: constructive stress test; Delta=0, regenerated under the frozen seed

methods.lr: likelihood-ratio plug-in against the two class mixtures; always answers
methods.ood: total-variation distance to the safe-class mixture, thresholded; always answers
methods.conformal: split-conformal label set from class-conditional nonconformity; Alert iff the set is not a singleton
methods.frontier: the LP-optimal randomized Certify/Alert/Reject rule at alpha=beta=0.05

fairness: Every baseline sees the full labelled registered class; nothing is held out from it that the frontier rule gets.

Every baseline is tuned twice and both tunings are reported: (a) to maximise its own balanced accuracy, and (b) to minimise its own worst-case unsafe-to-Certify error. Tuning (b) exists so that the comparison is not a criterion mismatch.
No baseline is tuned to fail, and no channel is dropped from the report.
metrics: wc_unsafe_certify = max over registered unsafe models of P(Certify)
wc_safe_reject    = max over registered safe models of P(Reject)
decisiveness      = min over registered models of P(not Alert)
balanced_accuracy over the registered class, the baselines' own objective

predictions_registered_in_advance.P1: The frontier rule satisfies wc_unsafe_certify <= alpha and wc_safe_reject <= beta on every channel. This is a validity check on the implementation, not a finding.
predictions_registered_in_advance.P2: On the collision channel the frontier rule's decisiveness is at most alpha+beta = 0.10.
predictions_registered_in_advance.P3: THE QUESTION. On the collision channel at least one baseline reports balanced accuracy well above chance while its worst-case unsafe-to-Certify error exceeds alpha, i.e. it does not notice that the channel cannot support the decision.
predictions_registered_in_advance.P4: THE FAIR ALTERNATIVE. If every baseline either abstains heavily or falls to near-chance accuracy on the collision channel, that is recorded as the baselines noticing, and the contribution claimed is narrowed from detection to explanation.

prohibited: Reporting only the channel or tuning where the gap is largest.
Tuning a baseline on the frontier rule's own worst-case objective and then calling the comparison fair without also reporting its own-objective tuning.
Reading a large worst-case error as evidence that the baseline is a bad predictor; it is evidence about a different criterion.
